To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a relativistic bubble of matter can be viewed as a point-like object with a single degree of freedom, namely the bubble's area, and (ii) the action functional of bubble dynamics is formally identical to the Einstein-Maaxwell action for a point-like object in a gravitational field

(i) the action functional of relativistic bubble dynamics is formally quite similar in structure to the action of Einstein-Maxwell theory; (ii) the gauge field of this theory, in the presence of a cosmological constant, generates a ``vacuum'' phase of the de Siter type with two effective and distinct values for the cosmological constant, one inside and the other outside the bubble wall.
``The vacuum tension of the Standard Model is equivalent to the cosmological constant of the de Siter phase of the universe''.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of singular layers of matter, such as cosmic strings, cosmic domain walls, cosmic bubbles, and hadronic bags, under the influence of volume tension and surface tension.
a new type of gauge theory of singular matter in the presence of a gravitational background.
the relativistic dynamics of a ``bubble'' or domain wall, a thin shell of matter that separates two distinct vacuum phases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the theory of bubble dynamics provides a natural and unified framework for the study of a variety of physical phenomena ranging from the very early stages of the evolution of the Universe to the confinement of quarks and gluon.
the action principle of relativistic bubble dynamics provides a unified description of the physics of the ``early universe'' and the ``hadronic bags''.
the action for bubble dynamics is a universal and fundamental action for the dynamics in the presence of vacuum tension effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the complete theory of bubble dynamics in curved spacetime, and that the formalism is of universal applicability to the study of the nucleation, growth and collapse of bubbles of matter in a wide variety of physical situations.

the theory of relativistic bubble dynamics, as formulated in this paper, provides a unified framework for the dynamics of the ``vacuum'' in the context of the standard model of strong and electroweak interactions.
we have developed a unified and consistent formalism for the description of the dynamics of a singular layer in curved spacetime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of a single degree of freedom in the presence of vacuum tension is a theory with a very rich mathematical structure and a wide range of physical applications.
the physics of bubble nucleation is a universal phenomenon that can be described in a unified manner by the same action functional.

a single action functional can describe both the dynamics of the ``bubble'' and the ``vacuum tension'' effects that are responsible for the confinement of quarks and gluon inside hadrons and of the ``inflaton'' responsible for the inflationary expansion of the universe.
